steps.instruction: Create a div container with an id of 'app' and add a heading element inside it with the text 'My Todo List'.
steps.hint: Use document.createElement to create the elements, set their properties, and append them to the document body.

steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add an input element and a button element for capturing new todo text. The input should have a placeholder attribute set to 'Enter a new todo' and the button should have text 'Add Todo'.
steps.hint: Place the input and button elements after the heading. Use <input> for the input field and <button> for the button.

steps.instruction: Inside your script, declare two variables: 'todos' as an empty array and 'currentInput' as an empty string.
steps.hint: Use 'let' or 'const' to declare variables. For example: 'let todos = []' and 'let currentInput = ""'.

steps.title: Create a function to add a new todo item
steps.instruction: In the <script> section, create a function named 'addTodo' that will handle adding new todos. The function should be empty for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Place it after your variable declarations.

successCriteria: The addTodo function is defined in the script section with the correct name.

steps.title: Create a function to delete a todo item
steps.instruction: Define a function named deleteTodo that takes an index parameter and removes the todo at that index from the todos array.
steps.hint: Inside the function, use the splice method on the todos array to remove one element at the given index.
steps.seedCode: My Todo List
steps.expectedOutcome: A deleteTodo function that can remove a todo from the array when called with an index.
successCriteria: The deleteTodo function is defined, takes an index parameter, and uses splice to remove an element from the todos array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the deleteTodo function. This implements the delete functionality (D in CRUD).
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the deleteTodo function, but it needs to properly remove an item from the todos array using the index parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The deleteTodo function isn't defined correctly. Make sure it takes an index parameter and removes the corresponding todo from the array.

steps.title: Create a function to toggle todo completion status
steps.instruction: In the <script> section, define a function named toggleTodo that takes an id parameter and toggles the completed property of the todo item with that id in the todos array.
steps.hint: You can use the todos array's findIndex method to locate the todo by id, then update its completed property to the opposite of its current value.
steps.seedCode: My Todo List
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleTodo function is defined that can update the completion status of a todo item.
successCriteria: The toggleTodo function is defined, takes an id parameter, and toggles the completed property of the matching todo item in the todos array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the toggleTodo function. This implements the update (U) part of CRUD, allowing users to mark todos as complete or incomplete.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the toggleTodo function, but it's not fully implemented. Make sure it takes an id parameter and toggles the completed property of the matching todo item.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTodo function is not defined correctly. It should take an id parameter and toggle the completed property of the todo item with that id in the todos array.

steps.title: Create a function to render the todo list
steps.instruction: Define a function named renderTodos that maps through the todos array and returns HTML for each todo item.
steps.hint: Inside the function, use the map method on the todos array to generate list items (<li>) for each todo.
steps.seedCode: My Todo List
steps.expectedOutcome: A renderTodos function that takes the todos array and returns HTML string for each todo item.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the renderTodos function to display the todo list.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the function uses the map method to generate HTML for each todo.

steps.title: Wire the add button to call the add function and update display
steps.instruction: Add an event listener to the add button that calls the addTodo function and then calls renderTodos to update the display.
steps.hint: Use addEventListener with 'click' event on the button element. Inside the listener, call addTodo() and then renderTodos().

steps.title: Wire the input field to update the current input state
steps.instruction: Add an event listener to the input field that updates the input state variable on each change. Use the 'input' event type.
steps.hint: You can add an event listener to the input element using addEventListener('input', function). Inside the function, update the input state variable with the current value from the input field.

steps.instruction: In your renderTodos function, modify the code that creates each todo list item to include a delete button and a toggle completion button.
steps.hint: Inside the loop where you create li elements, add two button elements after the todo text. Give them appropriate text like 'Delete' and 'Toggle'.

steps.title: Wire delete and toggle buttons to their respective functions
steps.instruction: Inside the renderTodos function, add event listeners to the delete and toggle buttons you created earlier. For the delete button, call deleteTodo with the todo's index. For the toggle button, call toggleTodo with the todo's index.
steps.hint: Use button.addEventListener('click', () => { ... }) for each button. Make sure to pass the correct index parameter to your functions.
